name: Navan
summary: Business travel and expense management in one. Book trips, automate expense reports and control spend with real-time visibility.
best_for: companies of up to 300 employees that want self-serve travel booking with built-in policy control, free on Navan Business, and optionally unified expense management on top
skip_if: your travel volume is a few trips a year (any booking site does), or you need expense-only tooling without the travel layer
honest_knock: 'Free' is real but has a mechanism: Navan earns commission on bookings made through its inventory, so the platform's incentive is that your travel flows through Navan, and pricing on specific routes/hotels deserves an occasional spot-check against direct booking. The free Business plan stops at 300 employees and lists corporate negotiated rates as an Enterprise feature; expense management is free for 5 users and $15 per user per month after that.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user a month from user 6
pricing.notes: (read 24 September 2026 and re-read 27 November 2026 on navan.com/pricing, unchanged) Navan Business is free for companies of up to 300 employees, with no limit on trips, and Navan Expense is free for the first 5 monthly expensing users and then $15 per user per month. Above 300 employees the plan is Navan Enterprise, priced by quote. An expensing user is anyone who submits a transaction in the month, so the expense bill follows who actually files, not headcount. The travel side is free because it is funded by travel-supplier commissions, which makes the question not what it costs but what it steers; note that corporate negotiated rates sit in the Enterprise column of the plan table, not the Business one. Our July and August 2026 readings found no amount on this URL and put the free expense threshold at 15 users; the page now says 5, and this text follows the page.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Navan on a free Business account that we created without a card. A business flight search took about 3 minutes and marked fares above the policy cap as out of policy. The account pricing page confirms the dossier: no cost for travel for companies of up to 300 employees, on a monthly term. No card was asked and nothing was booked. Account and start: a first attempt at 12:48 found no account yet and recorded the sign-up screens: an e-mail to verify, a choice of solution, and Create your company account with name, company, location, annual travel budget in USD, role and a password, with no card field, no phone field and no call wall. We then created the account without a card. Our AI assistant ran the second session in our browser, in its own tab, on 19 November 2026 from about 14:35 to 14:54. The traveller side was in English (UK); the admin side was switched from Dutch to English (United States) before the screenshots. Core action, a business flight search with the policy check, nothing booked: Business travel, Flights, Amsterdam to London return, Thursday 10 to Friday 11 December, 1 traveller. After Search a window suggested the train (Choosing train travel over air); we chose Continue with flights. Results came after about 8 seconds: 305 of 441 results with the 1 stop max filter, Nonstop only (17) from €160, and a line €654 and up is out of policy. The cheapest was British Airways BA 431, nonstop 1h 20m, Basic €160, Plus €180, Club Plus €450 with an out-of-policy icon; a filter shows In-policy fares only (187). The first results took about 3 minutes and 6 steps. Book was not clicked. The travel policy assigned by the admin: Maximum price for this search is €654, cabin max Economy, refundable and non-changeable fares allowed, cabin upgrades not allowed, and Your manager or travel approver will review, and may cancel, out-of-policy bookings. The policy edit page stayed blank after two reloads, so the policy was only read, not changed. An onboarding guide lists a 4-step plan (legal entity, team, travel policy, payment method) and $500 in Navan Rewards for 3+ employees, 3+ trips and $1,000+ spend within 30 days. Plans: Admin, Settings, Pricing says Plan: Unlimited trips every month with $0 trip fees. There's no cost to use Navan Travel., Monthly, renews on the 1st of every month, effective Nov 19, 2026, available only to companies with 300 or fewer employees and only on a monthly term. The public pricing page shows Navan Business, For companies up to 300 employees, Free, with expense features Free for the first 5 users, and Navan Enterprise behind Let's talk. Checkout: there is no checkout for the free plan. No card was asked at any point; Settings, Payments and the payment method step were not opened, and the expense module and the Navan card were not visible in this account. Cancelling: not done. Admin, Settings, Overview has no button to cancel or delete the account; the term is monthly and renews on the 1st, and how to end it was not established. Not tested: changing the policy (page stayed blank), hotels, the expense module, the card, a legal entity, inviting the team, a payment method and booking. Clean up: the account and the search stay; nothing was booked. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The policy edit page stayed blank in our session. The admin side opened in Dutch and had to be switched to English. There is no button to cancel or delete the account in the admin settings.
